$about: THE PER-ROUTE PERFORMANCE BUDGET — Phase 40. This file is the single source for every number
in it: the guards in scripts/perf/ read it, Lighthouse CI asserts against it, and
docs/ops/PERFORMANCE.md renders it. A number that lives in two places is a number that will
disagree with itself, so nothing here is repeated anywhere else.
`firstLoadJsKb` IS A TARGET, NOT A DESCRIPTION. It is the figure PHASE-39-46.md fixed for the
route. Where the site does not meet it today the gap is real, named in PERFORMANCE.md and
tracked — it is not quietly raised to whatever was measured. What stops the site drifting
further in the meantime is perf/bundle-baseline.json, which records what each route actually
weighs and fails CI on growth beyond 5%.
`islands` IS A CEILING AND IT IS SET AT THE MEASURED COUNT. Unlike bytes, an island count of
'2' on a route that has 7 would be red on every run from the day it was written, which trains
people to ignore the gate. The phase document's island numbers were written before Phase 10
gave the site a shell and Phase 23 put search in it; every public route now inherits five
islands it did not choose. Each route below records the measured figure, and `note` says what
the phase document asked for where the two differ.
RAISING ANY NUMBER HERE IS THE POINT OF THE FILE. It is a one-line edit a reviewer sees, with
a reason beside it. That is the whole mechanism: the budget is not advisory because exceeding
it fails CI, and it is not a straitjacket because changing it is one line.

coreWebVitals.$about: Site-wide, at the 75th percentile, on a Moto G4 / Slow 4G lab profile.

viewer3d.$about: The WebGL viewer, measured separately and never part of a first load. Asserted by scripts/perf/check-bundle.mjs against the module graph and by tests/e2e/model-viewer.spec.ts against the running site.

/about.note: The phase document budgets 2 islands. The shell contributes five to every public route (error copy, mega menu, mobile nav, search box, vitals reporter) and the section registry adds two more; none of the seven is chosen by this route.

/product/[slug].note: The only public route that meets its byte budget today, and the reason is instructive: it does not render CMS sections, so it never reaches the section registry.

/journal.note: Text-led, and the tightest byte budget on the site after /faq. The phase document budgets 2 islands.

/journal/category/[slug].note: Five, not seven: this route renders its own listing rather than CMS sections, so it carries the shell and nothing else. It and /search are the two lightest routes on the site, which is the measurement that identified the section registry as the cost.

/search.note: Shell only — no CMS sections. See /journal/category/[slug].

/studio.$about: A staff tool, authenticated and never indexed, so it is budgeted as one surface rather than as eighty-two routes — which is also what the phase document does. No LCP target: nothing here is a landing page.

excluded./design-system: A development-only gallery under app/(devtools), not reachable in production and not a visitor surface.
excluded./design-system/[group]: A development-only gallery under app/(devtools), the per-group view of /design-system. Not reachable in production and not a visitor surface.
